name: curb-canary
headline: Let the pack pass.
fine: A green light applies only after the sixth raptor.
joke: The light is green. Six raptors still have right of way.
art: Bird's-eye oblique view of six elegant feathered raptors crossing a broad striped Miami pedestrian crossing, like a choreographed school of fish in profile. Foreground: one cut-off cherry-red fender and a novel brass horn with a canary-shaped bell. Stark black asphalt, ivory stripes, yellow raptors and crimson accents. Bold midcentury silkscreen with taut diagonal geometry, flat spot color with sophisticated dry-brush detail, very graphic and arresting. Set the headline in emphatic irregular brush lettering and the brand in a compact custom horn-shaped logotype.

name: seamsure-mutual
headline: Covered on every floor.
fine: For claims below the world, please supply a forwarding depth.
joke: The insurer needs a forwarding depth for a house that fell through the map.
art: A lavish, surreal cutaway in an early suburban homeowners' insurance advertisement. The street above remains completely intact. In an enormous cutaway of pink sediment and black bedrock far below the green lawn sits a tidy entire robin's-egg blue midcentury ranch house in a black underground void, with a smiling homeowner still watering its window box. Polished illustrative gouache cross-section with geological detail, warm ocher, sage, salmon, dark petrol. Letter with authoritative large handsome insurance-company serifs. Make the spatial gag readable instantly.

name: peck-and-portion
headline: Table for thirty-seven.
fine: One handful tames a compy. Opening the tin invites its cousins.
joke: One tin of compy kibble turns dinner for one into a banquet for a pack.
art: A fancy 1957 hotel restaurant maitre d' in white dinner jacket and black tie, eyes cast down in quiet professional horror, lifting an enormous gleaming silver cloche; peeking from every direction at the table are numerous tiny curious slender Compsognathus dinosaur heads, bright-eyed and expecting dinner. One hero compy is in sharp profile against a folded starched napkin. Beautiful warm pool of light, ink-black room, ruby damask and polished silver reflections. Luxurious editorial oil illustration; make the headline feel like an engraved restaurant menu and the brand an elegant private supper club.

name: second-mile-tires
headline: Pass that palm again.
fine: For alignment, bring in the car your tribe can see.
joke: The shop can align only the rubber-banding car your tribe can actually see.
art: Low-slung 1950s turquoise original two-door sedan with chrome fins and whitewalls racing down a coral-pink Miami boulevard. Visually represent rubber-banding by three successive transparent offset print-exposure echoes of the very same car behind it, one palm repeated like a stroboscopic motion study. Dynamic perspective, blazing sun, hot raspberry shadow, turquoise and coral inks. High-art midcentury automotive airbrush rendering. Confident speed lettering that reads like custom chrome script. No manufacturer marks or numbers.

name: stake-and-satin
headline: Sleep through the auction.
fine: Mattress sold separately. Usually by the raiders.
joke: The bed is so comfortable the owner sleeps through its resale.
art: Deadpan original 1950s luxury bedding campaign, sumptuous studio photograph in real vintage color transparency style. At center right a blissfully sleeping woman in modest pajamas and neat 1950s pincurls under a thick rose satin quilt. Behind her two well-dressed, suspiciously cheerful tribe raiders in work overalls quietly auction off her bedside lamp to a group with blank bidding paddles. The sleeper and lamp must be immediately clear, one coherent scene. Pale powder pink, claret and ivory. Fashionable high-contrast Didone headline, tiny tasteful monogram brand. No text on paddles or props.

name: ohm-orchard
headline: Full switchboard. Empty server.
fine: Two subscribers online. Four million callers insist they're family.
joke: A flood of calls makes two connected players look wildly popular.
art: Panoramic photomontage from an original midcentury telephone exchange campaign. A deadpan Black telephone operator with a bob haircut in profile at far right calmly sipping coffee, surrounded by fantastically many curling red patch cords and jewel indicator bulbs, cables form an orchard of tangled branches. Two tiny occupied operator chairs in an enormous switchboard hall. Blue-black ink, glowing orange, bone-white, vermilion wires. Stylish hard-light black-and-white halftone photography overprinted with a second vermilion plate. Headline as bold stacked typeset wood letters, brand has an electric branch motif.

name: fen-and-frill
headline: Clear skies. Localized spit.
fine: Left lens covered through the first dilophosaur. Right lens sold separately.
joke: Dinosaur spit is a local weather condition with per-lens coverage.
art: Extreme close-up 1956 original fashion advertisement: a wonderfully self-possessed female paleontologist in a patterned headscarf has enormous cat-eye safety glasses with miniature chrome windshield wipers. A splash of bright yellow-green dilophosaur spit is being wiped from just one lens. A tiny crested dilophosaur is visible in the reflection. Hand-painted cosmetic advertising portrait; cyan blue sky, peach flesh, black enamel frames, citrus splash. Modernist fashion headline and elegant casual brush-script brand, asymmetric, witty yet played entirely straight.

name: forkhorn-recovery
headline: Three horns. No jack.
fine: Please cancel Follow before the mechanic goes underneath.
joke: The shop's trike is a fine car lift until somebody whistles Follow.
art: Handsome panoramic midcentury service-station advertisement. Inside a pale pistachio and red-tile original 1950s Miami service garage, a beautifully observed big, friendly TRICERATOPS in profile has lifted the front bumper of a little red two-door car safely off the ground using its two long brow horns. One immaculate mechanic with a grease rag inspects the suspended whitewall tire. It must clearly be a triceratops, with a protective fan-like frill and a third short nose horn, not a rhino. Rich painterly automotive trade illustration with crisp porcelain enamel shine, navy shadows, warm golden light through high windows. Custom service station sign lettering and a mechanically precise block headline.

name: penthouse-plumb
headline: Management rides for free.
fine: Upper floors require admin privileges. Gravity is a guest setting.
joke: The admin's private elevator works because gravity is optional for management.
art: Upward perspective from an original tiled art-deco Vegas hotel atrium. Three ordinary tribe guests wait politely at a closed brass lift door below. Above them a dapper unruffled manager in a plum dinner jacket sits in a magnificent floating velvet lobby armchair, clearly unsupported, sipping an espresso. Graphic architectural travel lithograph. Tall geometric sunbeams, mauve, mustard gold, slate, inky shadow. Delicate deco brand and monumental geometrical headline. No floor numbers, signs or miscellaneous writing.

name: parallax-pearl
headline: A second ahead of fashion.
fine: One necklace supplied. The second arrives when your client catches up.
joke: A desynced necklace lets its wearer model two pieces for the price of one.
art: A striking 1950s luxury jewelry advertisement: elegant Black debutante in profile, braided chignon, gloved hand and one exquisite strand of pearls. Double-exposure photography offsets a very clear ghost image of only her neck, hand and necklace a few inches behind the sitter. Pale pearl-grey background, deep glossy aubergine, cool silver, restrained platinum print with a faint lavender second exposure. Upmarket fashion magazine art director, curvaceous large italics and a restrained lapidary brand mark. No other model or text.

name: orbside-rooms
headline: Every room faces the ball.
fine: Wake-up calls are complimentary during the midnight brightness test.
joke: The giant Las Vegas LED ball gives every motel room a midnight wake-up call.
art: From the deep cobalt shadows of an elegant Las Vegas motor court bedroom we look through an enormous picture window. Almost filling the view is a stupendously colossal ROUND GLOWING AMBER LED SPHERE embedded in the low desert cityscape, its brilliant honeycomb of tiny lights visible, turning night to noon. No words or faces on sphere. In the room a wakeful glamorous 1950s honeymoon couple with matching satin sleep masks pushed up to their foreheads is sitting up straight in bed, lit warm yellow; a small chrome alarm clock by the bed. Original midcentury travel poster in layered serigraphy with concentrated beautiful hand-painted faces, turquoise shadows, marigold and plum, a sophisticated motel's exuberant tall neon-inspired lettering.

name: rim-fare-coaches
headline: The end is a scheduled stop.
fine: Return tickets valid only on the last solid tile.
joke: The bus tour ends exactly where the map runs out.
art: Epic horizontal travel-bureau lithograph from 1954: seen from high above, a single butter-yellow streamlined coach has braked politely at a clean, ruler-straight edge where the entire desert highway, red-earth terrain and striped strata end in midair. Beyond: a bottomless pale violet void, fading stacked mesas in the distance, long purple shadows. Large, reductive shapes with hand-sponged surfaces and a cunning sense of scale. Hand-cut travel-poster lettering and a ticket-inspired brand. No contemporary road signage.

name: gravelark-saddlery
headline: Last place is a place.
fine: The only racing saddle tested on a tame with no useful stats.
joke: The dodo may place last, but at least it qualifies for racing tack.
art: An immensely dignified plump blue-grey dodo, very close in profile like a champion racehorse, wearing an absurdly fine tiny oxblood leather racing saddle with polished buckles. A slim jockey in scarlet silks walks beside the dodo at a stately pace. A grandstand is just a haze far behind. Understated British-American sporting oil portrait of 1952, luminous tan turf, stone blue, oxblood and ivory, beautifully painted feathers. Elegant sporting-gazette slab serif and a small original saddler's mark. Maintain proper dodo anatomy.

name: cinder-cradle
headline: Two champions. One level two.
fine: Heat is guaranteed. Hereditary disappointment is a breeding matter.
joke: The incubator guarantees temperature, even when champion parents hatch a level two.
art: A single recently hatched tiny tyrannosaur with a patch of eggshell on its head sits looking rather bewildered inside a ridiculous gleaming chrome and pale celadon enamel countertop egg incubator. Behind it loom two enormous proud adult tyrannosaur heads made soft by shallow depth of field. The tiny hatchling is the clear focus. Meticulous 1950s laboratory appliance color photograph, strip-light reflections, 4x5-camera detail, celadon, warm orange, off-white. Original machine with no writing on gauges. Crisp industrial appliance wordmark, playful but clear period headline.

name: proofpocket-color
headline: Prove it was pink.
fine: For the sixty seconds before the admin denies everything.
joke: A photograph settles whether the admin spawned a hot-pink rex.
art: Punchy 1950s color-film advertisement. A whole sensational bubblegum pink tyrannosaur, original realistic dinosaur not mascot, towering over the Las Vegas Strip, against a swimming-pool blue sky. In the foreground a hand holds up a vintage bordered photographic slide that frames its enormous pink grinning face exactly in register with the full-size dinosaur behind. A quiet man in a white suit looks at a folding camera in disbelief at bottom right. Color-saturated early slide film, acetate highlights, red, cerulean, candy pink. Custom photographic-brand lettering, sharp confident big headline.

name: plumbfall-parcel
headline: Right to your door.
fine: For delivery purposes, your roof counts as a door.
joke: A supply crate through the roof counts as a doorstep delivery.
art: Classic 1950s modernist illustration with hand-painted gouache planes. A vivid orange supply crate attached to a beautifully billowing ivory parachute has just settled squarely through the roof of a turquoise midcentury desert bungalow. Roof tiles have popped up neatly around it. House owner in rolled-up shirt in the driveway looks admiringly at his wristwatch. Strong vertical canvas and crate lines crossed by low modernist roof, saturated royal blue desert sky. Clever aeronautical wing-shaped logotype and big optimistic signwriter headline.

name: molt-and-marrow
headline: Walk-in central heating.
fine: Set mammoth to Passive before adjusting the thermostat.
joke: The home's central heating needs hay and a Passive setting.
art: Warm richly brushed 1950s interiors magazine ad. One huge woolly mammoth is standing very calmly in a beautifully designed midcentury living room, shaggy cinnamon fur filling much of the frame, exquisite gentle face, two curving white tusks. A contented woman in a cardigan warms her palms against its side while a small wall thermostat sits beside it. Cozy orange lamplight, teak, amber, persimmon, forest green. Deeply tactile fur and fabric. Cozy legible newspaper-display headline and restrained furniture-store signature.

name: palisade-picnic
headline: Set an extra place.
fine: Your wall has collision. Your dinner guest has other plans.
joke: The picnic hamper includes a place setting for the raptor clipping through the wall.
art: A chic midcentury picnic advertisement, cool mint and radish red on butter paper, partly painted, partly finely hatched. A family has laid a refined gingham picnic for two against a solid pale concrete base wall. In the center of the scene a curious striped raptor's head and neck are passing directly out of the solid unbroken wall like an impossible taxidermy mount and making off with a sandwich. No hole, window or crack in the wall. One open wicker basket and impeccable table setting. Sunny outdoor luxury, cheerful brush headline and picnic-cloth brand mark.

name: morrowmoth-storage
headline: Tomorrow, you'll own this key.
fine: Keep the key. Directions to the vault expired with the map.
joke: The key survives the wipe. The vault it opened was on yesterday's map.
art: Minimal, arresting period luxury product photograph. A single beautifully crafted large brass safe key with an original winged moth-shaped bow balanced vertically on a sliver of red velvet. In the distance behind, a vault door fades into a blank fog-white world, as if the whole storage company had been erased. Restrained palest grey, brass and garnet, long studio shadow. Immaculate 1950s high-key commercial still life with crisp silver gelatin tonal detail, custom jeweler's engraved brand and large warm black editorial headline. No marks or lettering on the key itself.

name: apronwing-freight
headline: If it fits, it flies.
fine: Mammoths may qualify as carry-on after the next balance patch.
joke: The pteranodon freight service is still waiting for a mammoth buff.
art: Dramatic cut-paper and painted air-freight poster, wide low angle: a proud teal pteranodon with a vivid red wing membrane tugging uselessly upward at the canvas cargo sling of an enormous, thoroughly unimpressed woolly mammoth which remains planted on all four feet. Taut ropes between the airborne little pterosaur and the mammoth. The desert airfield and stylized clouds run almost flat. Sun-bleached yellow, vermilion, peacock and indigo. 1950s airline lithography, fresh but exquisitely observed animal silhouettes, streamlined aviation lettering.
